info.title: Aggregator DPG API
info.description: Aggregator BFF for the Blue Dots / Purple Dots networks — handles aggregator registration, brand + network config, public participant onboarding (link + bulk), and the dashboard rollup proxy to signalstack.

get.summary: Liveness probe
get.description: Returns 200 as long as the process is up — used by Docker healthcheck.

get.summary: Readiness probe
get.description: Returns 200 only when Postgres and Redis are both reachable; 503 otherwise.

post.summary: Register a coordinator from an invite
post.description: Creates the invited coordinator as `pending` with a Keycloak user that can sign in but holds no access yet. The email must be the invited address. The account becomes active when the invitee signs in with an email code and calls `POST /v1/user/activate`; no owner approval. Reached with the web BFF service-account token.

get.summary: Read a coordinator invite for its registration page
get.description: Checks the invite link without using it up and returns the invited email and the org it is for. Reached with the web BFF service-account token.

post.summary: Prune registrations stuck pending past token expiry + grace
Register an organisation from an invite
post.description: Creates the invited org under the inviting org as `pending`, with its Keycloak group and an owner user that can sign in but holds no access yet. The owner email must be the invited address. The org becomes active when the owner signs in with an email code and calls `POST /v1/user/activate`; no approval. 409 ORG_DEPTH_LIMIT, ORG_CHILD_LIMIT or ORG_TOTAL_LIMIT when the inviting org can no longer take it. Reached with the web BFF service-account token.

get.summary: Read an organisation invite for its registration page
get.description: Checks the invite link without using it up and returns the invited email and the inviting org. Reached with the web BFF service-account token.

get.summary: Read the caller aggregator profile
get.description: Returns the full aggregator row + brand + contact + status for the aggregator bound to the Bearer token claim.

patch.description: Partial update of the caller aggregator (name / contact). Consent is read-only after registration: a body carrying `consent` is refused with 400 SCHEMA_VALIDATION. Contact phone + email are mirrored to Keycloak before the DB write. Org details (url, locations, contact.company, contact.gstNumber) belong to the coordinator's organisation and are refused with 409 ORG_DETAILS_READ_ONLY.

get.summary: The signed-in user: kind, organisations and network-admin flag
Whether the signed-in user still has to accept the current terms
get.description: A coordinator accepts for itself; an org owner accepts for each org it owns, other than the root and the Default org. `org_ids` lists the owned orgs still to accept.

post.summary: Record that the signed-in user accepted the current terms
post.description: Records an acceptance of the shown terms and privacy versions for the caller (a coordinator) or for each org it owns that has not accepted yet, all or nothing. `recorded` is 0 when nothing was outstanding. Versions that are no longer current answer 409 `CONSENT_VERSION_CHANGED` and record nothing.

get.summary: One coordinator within reach

post.summary: Coordinators within reach, newest first
post.description: Filters by org, status and served domain; an org outside reach yields an empty page. An owner sees the coordinators of the organisations it owns only, not those of their child organisations. Keyset paged by an opaque cursor.

post.summary: Invite coordinators into an organisation
post.description: Mints and mails a 14-day invite per address (the invitee registers and consents themselves). The Default org takes no invites. An address already registered in this org is reported under `existing`; any other existing account is mailed a sign-in note and counted as sent.

post.summary: List the unused coordinator invites of an organisation
post.description: Invites nobody has registered with yet, newest first, keyset paged. `expired` invites no longer work. An invitee who registered is a coordinator (`POST /v1/user/search`), pending until they verify their email.

post.summary: Activate the caller's invited account
post.description: Called by the portal right after an invitee's first sign-in. The account must come from an invite (`decision_made = invited`) and the sign-in must have verified the email (an email code). Runs the approve step without its mail and tells the inviting organisation's owner; an invited organisation becomes active with its owner. Already active answers 200 with `activated: false`. The caller refreshes its token afterwards to pick up the new access.

post.summary: Add the signed-in owner to the team of an organisation they own
post.description: Creates the owner's own coordinator account in `org_id` on the owner's contact and sign-in, and approves it at once. `serves` lists one or more network domain ids. `consent` is the coordinator Terms and Privacy consent, the same block as `POST /v1/user/invite/accept`; it is recorded in the consent ledger with the account. The owner's Keycloak user is not changed. Refused for the Default org, an org that is not active, an org the caller does not own, and any owner of the network root. One coordinator account per person: a second self-add answers 409, except that a deactivated account in the same org is reactivated.

patch.description: `serves` lists one or more network domain ids. The coordinator's Keycloak `aggregator_type` attribute is written first, then, for an approved coordinator, the Signals organisation's domains. The coordinator's sessions are then ended, so its next login carries the new types.

get.summary: One organisation within reach, with its owner and coordinator counts
get.description: An owner also reads, read-only, the direct children of its own organisations, and nothing deeper; the owner contact of such an organisation is masked, except to the parent's owner while the organisation is pending. The network admin reads the top-level organisations the same way. For such an organisation coordinator_count, pending_count and child_count are 0. The fields query adds data that is left out by default. fields=known_as_values adds org.known_as_values: the values the organisation defines for its direct children, or null when it cannot have child organisations (the Default organisation, or an organisation at max_depth). fields=parent.known_as_values adds org.parent: the parent's id, name and stored known_as_values list ([] when it has none), which holds the choices for this org's known_as (the list, or only "aggregator" when it is empty). org.parent is null unless the caller owns the parent (the network admin for a top-level organisation), and for the root, the Default organisation and a rejected organisation. An unknown name in fields answers 400 SCHEMA_VALIDATION.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of extra data to include: known_as_values, parent.known_as_values.

post.summary: Organisations within reach, by name
post.description: An owner sees the organisations it owns and, read-only, their direct children; nothing deeper. The network admin owns the network, so it sees the top-level organisations. With `parent_id` set to an org within reach, lists that org's direct children. For an org the caller does not own, coordinator_count, pending_count and child_count are 0. `descendants_of` lists the orgs below an org within reach, limited to the same reach. The two cannot be sent together. Filters by status and a case-insensitive name prefix; keyset paged by an opaque cursor.

patch.description: Every field, the name included, is the org's owner's only (the slug never changes); the network admin views other owners' orgs but does not edit them (403). known_as changes through PATCH /v1/org/known-as/update/:id and the parent through PATCH /v1/org/parent/update/:id. The Default org's details are not editable. `profile` changes fields of the deployment's org-registration schema (e.g. website, GST number, domains): only fields marked x-updatable, checked against that schema; null removes a field. A bad field answers 400 with fields.field_errors and saves nothing. Locations, legal name, website and GST number are rendered for every coordinator of the org; description is shown in the console only.

patch.summary: Set what an organisation is known as, or the "known as" values it defines for the organisations under it
patch.description:
The body has exactly one of known_as or known_as_values. An organisation the caller cannot see answers 404.

known_as sets the organisation's own value. Only the owner of the organisation's parent sets it: the network admin for a top-level organisation, else the owner of the parent organisation (an active organisation it owns); anyone else gets 403. known_as must be a key of the parent's list, or aggregator when that list is empty (400 SCHEMA_VALIDATION with fields.known_as otherwise). The network, the Default organisation and a rejected organisation answer 409, and so does an organisation moved while the request ran (fields.reason: moved). The organisation's owner is emailed when it is not the caller. Sending the current value answers 200 with the organisation unchanged and sends no email.

known_as_values replaces the whole list the organisation defines for its direct children, and the response adds the saved known_as_values with every key set. Only the organisation's owner sets it (an active organisation it owns; the network's list for the network admin): 403 when the caller sees but does not own it, 409 for the Default organisation. An entry that is already saved sends its key back and keeps it; a new entry sends only a name, and the API makes its key from the name. A key that is not already in the list answers 400 SCHEMA_VALIDATION (fields.known_as_values: unknown_key, fields.index). At most one entry is the default; new organisations under this one get it, else aggregator. Organisations under this one whose value leaves the list take the default, else aggregator; a renamed entry keeps its key, so they keep it too.

patch.summary: Move an organisation under a new parent (network admin)
patch.description: Moves the organisation and every organisation below it; their depths follow. The org must be pending or active, not the Default org. The parent must be the network or an active organisation, not the org or one below it, with room for another child, and the moved orgs must stay within max_depth. The moved org keeps its known_as when the new parent's list has it; otherwise it takes the new parent's default value, else aggregator. Organisations below it keep theirs. The owner is told when the org moved.

get.summary: Candidate parents for moving an organisation (network admin)
get.description: Every org that could be the new parent, the network first, each with the result a move there would give: ok, or the refusal code in reason (INVALID_PARENT, PARENT_CYCLE, CHILD_LIMIT, DEPTH_LIMIT, or NOT_MOVABLE). subtree_size counts the orgs that move.

post.summary: Invite organisations to register under an organisation
post.description: Mints and mails a 14-day invite per address to register an organisation under `parent_id`: the root for the network admin, else an active organisation the caller owns. The invitee registers, then verifies the invited email with a one-time code; there is no approval step. 409 ORG_DEPTH_LIMIT, ORG_CHILD_LIMIT or ORG_TOTAL_LIMIT when the parent cannot take another organisation. An address that already has an account is mailed a sign-in note and counted as sent.

post.summary: List the unused organisation invites of an organisation
post.description: Invites to register under `parent_id` that nobody has used yet, newest first, keyset paged: the root for the network admin, else an organisation the caller owns. `expired` invites no longer work. An invited organisation that registered is in `POST /v1/org/search`, pending until its owner verifies the email.

post.summary: Re-apply an active organisation's owner sign-in access (its parent's owner)
post.description: Only the owner of the organisation's parent repairs it: the network admin for a top-level organisation, else the owner of the parent organisation. Anyone else gets 404. Enables the owner's Keycloak user, grants the org_owner role and adds them to the org's group. Idempotent.

get.summary: The network, its "known as" values and the tree limits (network admin)
get.description: Read-only. The network, the tree limits from the instance config, and how many pending and active organisations count toward max_total_orgs. Depth 1 sits directly under the network. fields=known_as_values adds network.known_as_values: the "known as" values the network defines for top-level organisations (edited through PATCH /v1/org/known-as/update/:id with known_as_values). An unknown name in fields answers 400 SCHEMA_VALIDATION.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of extra data to include: known_as_values.

get.summary: Every role and its permissions
A user's roles and the additional roles the caller may assign

post.summary: Assign an additional role to a user in an organisation
post.description: Needs the role's assigned_by permission in that organisation. Replaces a live assignment of the same role there. Refused for a base role, an organisation the user is not part of, yourself, the wrong account or organisation type, separation of duties, and beyond the role's longest validity.

post.summary: Revoke a user's additional role in an organisation
Create a custom role from existing permissions
Delete a custom role no live assignment uses

get.summary: Every role the API enforces (network admin, read-only)
Every permission in the catalogue (network admin, read-only)
Download the bulk-upload template (CSV or XLSX)
get.description: Both formats are generated from the participant schema resolved out of network.json for ?participant_type= (seeker/provider), and both are gated on the caller's registered aggregator_type. ?format=csv (default) returns text/csv: the header row plus one example row. ?format=xlsx returns a four-tab workbook for that type — instructions, allowed values, worked sample rows and an empty grid with dropdowns on every closed-set column. Array-typed fields use the network's csv_array_delimiter. Responds with a file attachment on 200 (no JSON body).

parameters.name: participant_type
parameters.description: Participant domain id declared by the active network (e.g. seeker, provider).

post.summary: Create a new bulk-upload job
post.description: Reserves a pending bulk-upload job for the caller aggregator and returns pre-signed upload instructions. The browser uploads CSV bytes directly to object storage, then calls /start. `participant_type` is validated against the active network config at request time.

participant_type.description: Participant domain id declared by the active network (e.g. seeker, provider).

upload_url.description: Deprecated: a signed PUT URL without the size limit; follow `upload` instead.

content_type.description: Deprecated: the content type is in `upload`.

get.summary: List bulk-upload jobs
get.description: Paginated list of bulk-upload jobs (newest first) for the caller aggregator. Uploads that were never started (`pending`, or failed as `upload_abandoned`) are left out.

post.summary: Start processing a pending bulk-upload job
post.description: Transitions a pending job to running; the worker onboards each valid row to signalstack. Idempotent on already-running/completed jobs.

attestation.description: Operator attestation of authority to upload.

get.summary: Read a bulk-upload job
get.description: Returns the full job row including status, per-row counters, and error summary.

get.summary: Download per-row error CSV
get.description: Returns a JSON payload carrying a short-lived pre-signed download URL for the errors.csv report (rows that failed validation/onboarding with reason + offending fields), plus the final counters. Only available once the upload is completed and at least one row failed.

post.summary: Create a shareable registration link
post.description: Creates a shareable registration link for the caller aggregator, scoped to a domain (seeker/provider). `domain` and `registration_mode` are validated against the active network config at request time. Drafts are metadata-only; status=live also mints the public URL. The QR is generated client-side from that URL (#650).

get.summary: List the voice bots a link in a domain can use
get.description: Voice bots configured for the domain, plus the key of the domain default (null when several bots serve it and none is the default). Feeds the bot picker on the link form.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Network domain id the link is for.

get.summary: List the caller aggregator's registration links
get.description: Paginated list (newest first) of registration links with status + counters.

patch.description: Partial update of mutable draft-link fields (slug, context, expiry). Only draft links can be edited; `registration_mode` and `domain` are immutable and unknown keys are rejected with 400.

get.summary: Read a registration link
get.description: Full link row including counters + status.

post.summary: Activate a registration link
post.description: Flips the link status to live so the public form accepts submissions and returns the public URL. Idempotent when already live; retired links cannot be reactivated (409).

post.summary: Deactivate a registration link
post.description: Flips status to retired — the public form returns 410 for further submissions. Idempotent when already retired.

get.summary: Resolve a public registration link
get.description: Looks up a live (non-expired, active) registration link by org slug + link slug. Returns the link metadata (domain, context, schema id) that the public registration form needs. 404 for missing/draft slugs, 410 for retired or expired ones.

schema.description: JSON Schema for the link's domain; null for account_only links.

identity.description: Identity field selectors (name / phone / email) for this domain.

offers.description: Registration channels the page offers, in display order.

voice_bot.description: The voice bot the link resolves to; null when it offers no voice option.

phone.description: The number the participant calls; shown before they register.

post.summary: Submit a public participant registration
post.description: Public endpoint reached by the QR-link registration form. Validates the submission against the link's domain schema (runtime Ajv — the body shape is dynamic per network/domain), then creates the user + profile in signalstack. Returns 201 on success, 409 (outcome:'skipped') when the identity is already owned by ANOTHER aggregator, and 429 when the per-link rate limit trips. There is no de-duplication within an aggregator: a repeat submission creates a new profile and returns 201.

schema.description: Dynamic registration payload validated at runtime against the link domain's participant JSON Schema (identity fields such as name/phone/email plus profile fields). consent_terms / consent_privacy are accepted on account_only links. item_locations optionally carries coordinates the registrant picked from the address autocomplete.

requestBody.description: Dynamic registration payload validated at runtime against the link domain's participant JSON Schema (identity fields such as name/phone/email plus profile fields). consent_terms / consent_privacy are accepted on account_only links. item_locations optionally carries coordinates the registrant picked from the address autocomplete.

post.summary: Get the voice-bot number of a public link, creating the account if new
post.description: Public endpoint behind the 'talk to the voice bot' option of a two-option link. Checks the phone with signalstack first: a new phone gets an account (no profile) under the link's aggregator; an existing one, whoever owns it, is left untouched. Returns the bot's number either way (200, never 409 for an existing account). 409 when the link offers no voice option or no bot resolves; 429 when the per-link rate limit, shared with the form submit, trips.

schema.description: The domain's identity name and phone keys, consent_terms / consent_privacy, and year_of_birth (or age) on guardian-gated domains. Phone is required; email and profile fields are rejected.

requestBody.description: The domain's identity name and phone keys, consent_terms / consent_privacy, and year_of_birth (or age) on guardian-gated domains. Phone is required; email and profile fields are rejected.

existing.description: True when the phone already had an account; nothing was created then.

get.summary: Probe an identity before opening the registration form
get.description: Anonymous identity probe used by the public registration form. Classifies the supplied email/phone as new (user_exists=false), an own user with optional lifecycle summary, or owned by another aggregator (owned_elsewhere=true). Requires at least one of email or phone_number, plus the network and domain to scope the signalstack probe.

get.summary: Aggregated onboarding totals
get.description: Sum of total / passed / failed / skipped onboarding attempts for the caller aggregator, optionally constrained by ?from=&to= ISO dates and narrowed to one profile type by ?domain=.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Profile type (network domain id) to count; omitted counts every profile type.

get.summary: Onboarding totals grouped by source
get.description: Per-source breakdown of onboarding counters for the caller aggregator (e.g. by_link / by_bulk_upload), optionally date-bounded by ?from=&to= and narrowed to one profile type by ?domain=.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Profile type (network domain id) to count; omitted counts every profile type.

get.summary: Aggregator dashboard rollup + items
get.description: Proxies signalstack's pre-computed dashboard payload (rollup + paginated participants + cursor + metadata) for the caller aggregator. by_domain[<id>] contains seeker/provider slices; refresh=true bypasses the TTL cache. The 200 payload is proxied verbatim from signalstack, so no response schema is pinned (avoids a deep zod re-parse of the rollup on every reply).

get.summary: CSV export of dashboard items
get.description: Returns a CSV (text/csv) of the dashboard items for the caller aggregator. Filters by optional status. Body is the CSV text, with Content-Disposition: attachment.

post.summary: CSV export of DECRYPTED profile data for selected items
post.description: Returns a CSV (text/csv) of decrypted profile data for the given item_ids, scoped to the caller aggregator. The signalstack admin key never leaves the server.

get.summary: Public brand + network config
get.description: Brand palette/logo + per-domain labels (tab name, plural, tiles, status_rules) + dashboard bucket labels. Web BFF reads this at boot to theme the portal and render the dashboard config-driven.

get.summary: Participant registration-link consent document
get.description: The participant `consent.json` (Terms / Privacy / profile-creation) fetched from `aggregator.network.consent_source` — the same cache-backed pull as network.json. `participant_consent` is null when no `consent_source` is configured (the web app then falls back to its on-disk copy). No auth — operator-controlled content shown on the public registration form.

get.summary: Whether the contact-support form is enabled
get.description: Reports whether SUPPORT_EMAIL is configured on this instance, plus the attachment limits and accepted content types. The web app hides the "Contact support" entry point when disabled, and validates files against these limits before uploading them.

post.summary: Send a contact-support message
post.description: Emails the submitted complaint/support request to SUPPORT_EMAIL (and SUPPORT_CC_EMAIL when set), with Reply-To set to the submitter email so support can reply directly. Each submission carries a SUP-YYYYMMDD-XXXXXX reference.

post.summary: Request an async participant PII export
post.description: Creates a durable campaign job that exports the participant contact fields (name/email/phone, each with profile/user provenance) for the given owned items to a private CSV, and emails a short-lived pre-signed download link to the requesting user. Body is the shared campaign envelope { item_ids, metadata[], content{} }. Send an Idempotency-Key header to make retries safe. Returns 202 { job_id }; poll GET /v1/campaign/export/{job_id} for status.

get.summary: List the org's export jobs (newest first)
get.description: Returns the requesting org's export jobs, newest first, with derived status counts. Cursor pagination — pass the returned next_cursor to page.

get.summary: Get one export job's status and per-item outcomes
get.description: Returns the job status (derived from item counts) and each item id with its status, provider ref and skip/error reason. Scoped to this org and to the export channel — a job belonging to another org or channel returns 403.

post.summary: Request an async voice-call campaign dispatch
post.description: Creates a durable campaign job that dispatches a Raya voice-call batch to the given owned items. Body is the shared campaign envelope { item_ids, metadata[], content{} } where content is the voice dispatch request (agent_id required; action is dispatch-only in v1). Send an Idempotency-Key header to make retries safe. Returns 202 { status, requested, job_id }; poll GET /v1/campaign/voice/{job_id} for status.

get.summary: List the org's voice jobs (newest first)
get.description: Returns the requesting org's voice jobs, newest first, with derived status counts. Cursor pagination — pass the returned next_cursor to page.

get.summary: Get one voice job's status and per-item outcomes
get.description: Returns the job status (derived from item counts) and each item id with its status, provider ref and skip/error reason. Scoped to this org and to the voice channel — a job belonging to another org or channel returns 403.

post.summary: Email owned participants (async)
post.description: Creates a durable campaign job that emails the given owned participants a shared message (subject + Markdown body, with an optional fixed set of {{placeholder}} tokens personalised per recipient). Body is the shared campaign envelope { item_ids, metadata[], content{subject, body_markdown, reply_to?} }. Recipient email addresses are resolved server-side and never returned. Send an Idempotency-Key header to make retries safe. Returns 202 { job_id }; poll GET /v1/campaign/email/{job_id} for per-recipient outcomes.

get.summary: List the org's email jobs (newest first)
get.description: Returns the requesting org's email jobs, newest first, with derived status counts. Cursor pagination — pass the returned next_cursor to page.

get.summary: Get one email job's status and per-item outcomes
get.description: Returns the job status (derived from item counts) and each item id with its status, provider ref and skip/error reason. Scoped to this org and to the email channel — a job belonging to another org or channel returns 403.

get.summary: Download the latest non-PII Signals dump
get.description: Returns a short-lived pre-signed URL for each file in CAMPAIGN_DUMP_FILES (default: user, items, item_actions, aggregators). URLs expire after CAMPAIGN_DUMP_URL_TTL_SECONDS. Requires the campaign-manager system token (client_credentials). Files differ in last_modified when the export was caught mid-run; re-fetch then. Files absent from S3 are listed in missing; 404 DUMP_NOT_AVAILABLE when none is present.
